:knowledge-point/_questions.:knowledge-point/title: Identifying Equilibrium Solutions of a Differential Equation

question.:question/problem:
Consider the differential equation

$$
\frac{dy}{dt} + \left(y + 1\right) = \left(y + 1\right) + \left(\left(y - 1\right)^{2} \ln{\left(y - 1 \right)} + e^{-2}\right).
$$

Which of the following are equilibrium solutions? Select all that apply.
question.:question/worked-solution:
A constant function $y(t)=c$ has derivative $dy/dt=0$. It must satisfy the original equation and its domain restrictions.

The original equation requires $y - 1>0$.

Isolating the derivative gives

$$
\frac{dy}{dt} = y^{2} \ln{\left(y - 1 \right)} - 2 y \ln{\left(y - 1 \right)} + \ln{\left(y - 1 \right)} + e^{-2}.
$$

Test each supplied constant in the original equation, with the derivative set to zero.

- For $y=c=2$, evaluate the non-derivative left and right sides, denoted $L(c)$ and $R(c)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}\ln{\left(c - 1 \right)} &= \ln{\left(1 \right)} \\  &= 0 \\ L(c) &= c + 1 \\  &= 3 \\ R(c) &= \left(c + 1\right) + \left(\left(c - 1\right)^{2} \ln{\left(c - 1 \right)} + e^{-2}\right) \\  &= e^{-2} + 3\end{aligned}
$$

The values differ, so this is *not* an equilibrium solution.

- For $y=c=1 + e$, evaluate the non-derivative left and right sides, denoted $L(c)$ and $R(c)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}\ln{\left(c - 1 \right)} &= \ln{\left(e \right)} \\  &= 1 \\ L(c) &= c + 1 \\  &= 2 + e \\ R(c) &= \left(c + 1\right) + \left(\left(c - 1\right)^{2} \ln{\left(c - 1 \right)} + e^{-2}\right) \\  &= e^{-2} + 2 + e + e^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

The values differ, so this is *not* an equilibrium solution.

- For $y=c=e^{-1} + 1$, evaluate the non-derivative left and right sides, denoted $L(c)$ and $R(c)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}\ln{\left(c - 1 \right)} &= \ln{\left(e^{-1} \right)} \\  &= -1 \\ L(c) &= c + 1 \\  &= e^{-1} + 2 \\ R(c) &= \left(c + 1\right) + \left(\left(c - 1\right)^{2} \ln{\left(c - 1 \right)} + e^{-2}\right) \\  &= e^{-1} + 2\end{aligned}
$$

The values agree, so this is an equilibrium solution.

Select $y=e^{-1} + 1$.
